developments.title: Inkling 2 Mini 26‑billion‑parameter model released for zero‑config local inference
detail: Inkling 2 Mini, a 26‑billion‑parameter looped transformer, is available as a 10 GB model that can run locally on a laptop with zero configuration.
The model is hosted on the Osaurus platform, allowing users to select and execute it directly without installing software.
It achieves a 20.1 score on the AA Index for agentic tasks.
developments.why_it_matters: This enables offline AI processing for sensitive data without relying on cloud services.

developments.title: macOS version of cc-switcher targets purpose-isolated subscriptions
detail: Greg Pstrucha created a macOS version of cc-switcher for workflows where subscriptions are kept purpose-isolated.
The implementation is intended for cases where CLIProxy is unnecessary, and users can point their agent at the repository to request setup.
It adapts the existing project to macOS rather than introducing a broader cross-platform rewrite.
developments.why_it_matters: Mac users with separate agent subscriptions can switch contexts without adopting CLIProxy.

developments.title: Quinn Slack trains a local "Hey Puck" wake-word model with Amp-generated data
detail: Quinn Slack reports training a local wake-word model that triggers on "Hey Puck," with the Amp coding agent generating the synthetic training data. The model was trained on 77.2 hours of Slack's own dictation recordings, with no training on other people's data.
Amp also helped gather recordings from additional microphones and built native Swift, Kotlin, and Web implementations of the wake word.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can hand a coding agent their own recordings and get a private cross-platform wake word without collecting any third-party training data.

developments.title: Vercel Labs deepsec uses glm‑flash for continuous local security scanning
detail: Vercel Labs’ deepsec tool is being run continuously with the local glm‑flash model to scan for security issues.
The setup has identified hundreds of vulnerabilities over a week, which are then handed off to an agent council using Theo’s tstack skill for remediation.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now run nonstop AI‑driven vulnerability detection locally, reducing reliance on cloud services and catching issues faster.

developments.title: LineShine supercomputer tops TOP500 and wins Gordon Bell Prize with domestic CPUs
detail: China’s LineShine supercomputer claimed the top spot on the TOP500 list at SC26 in Chicago, delivering 2.198 exa‑FLOPS, 21 % faster than the US El Capitan system and 26 % ahead on the real‑world HPCG benchmark.

The machine, built on domestic 304‑core LX2 CPUs with 4 TB/s on‑package HBM, also won the 2026 Gordon Bell Prize after solving the FeMoco chemistry benchmark in 105 minutes, marking the first major AI‑related award earned without any US‑origin silicon.
developments.why_it_matters: Researchers can now explore AI workloads on fully domestic hardware, reducing reliance on US chips and mitigating export‑control risks.

developments.title: AWS Lambda adds GPU support for running LLMs
detail: AWS announced that its Lambda serverless platform now supports GPU execution, enabling users to run large language models (LLMs) inside Lambda functions.
The new capability lets inference workloads be executed on‑demand without provisioning dedicated GPU servers, simplifying deployment for AI applications.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can now deploy GPU‑accelerated LLM inference in serverless Lambda functions, reducing latency and infrastructure overhead.

developments.title: Ray Fernando shares a /poteto-mode prompt for repo gardening
detail: Ray Fernando shared a prompt for using /poteto-mode on a repository. It first has an agent read the git history, past bug fixes, and review comments to identify mistakes that humans and other agents repeatedly make. It then directs the agent to eliminate those mistakes one at a time, preferring architectural changes first, then types, then a lint rule whose error message names the fix, then a test. It also asks to delete comments that merely restate code and to encode meaningful constraints with /no-comments. For concurrency, retries, or state machines, it instructs creating a formal verification skill with /create-formal-verification-skill, writing a model that replays an actual past bug and fails on it, and running that model in CI. It replaces unit tests that pin implementation details with those formal models plus real database and end-to-end tests, while keeping every test that guards security or legal behavior. Each step is shipped as one verifiable pull request, and every new check must catch a real past mistake before it is trusted.
developments.why_it_matters: Because each check must reproduce a real past mistake before it is trusted, teams can avoid adopting checks that only pass on current code.

developments.title: LingSante-3.1-flash model released with leading healthcare benchmark scores
detail: AntLing announced the release of LingSante-3.1-flash, an open‑weight mixture‑of‑experts model with 560 B total parameters and 25 B activations per token. The model achieves top results on several medical benchmarks, scoring 65.72 on HealthBench Professional, 72.22 on HLE with tools, and 94.10 on BrowseComp, surpassing Claude Opus 5.5, GPT‑6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon.
The weights are publicly available, enabling users to run the model on their own servers for privacy‑preserving medical applications such as EHR‑Complex and long‑horizon physician workflows.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now run a high‑performing, open‑weight medical model locally, keeping patient data private.

developments.title: OpenAI’s “Perplexity and Intelligence” essay proposes shared pretraining safety limits
detail: OpenAI released “Perplexity and Intelligence,” an essay that provides greater transparency into its pretraining progress and proposes common safety limits based on perplexity and other measurements. The essay links progress beyond those limits to the ability to understand AI behavior, aiming to establish shared safety bars across the AI community.
developments.why_it_matters: Researchers can compare OpenAI’s disclosed pretraining progress against the proposed limits before supporting further progress beyond them.

developments.title: Perfloop merges 150 changes across 36 open‑source projects
detail: Perfloop has surpassed 150 merged changes, reaching 155 as of today, spanning 36 different open‑source projects. The first 50 changes took 88 days, the next 50 took 42 days, and the last 50 were completed in just 20 days.
Initially focused on performance, the effort now includes bug fixes for half of the merged changes, covering major components like Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Elasticsearch.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can apply these performance improvements and recent bug fixes to their own deployments of Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, or Elasticsearch.

developments.title: LingSante-3.1-air-VL released as 124B MIT-licensed multimodal medical model
detail: Ant Ling released LingSante-3.1-air-VL, an open MIT-licensed multimodal medical model with 124 billion total parameters, 5.5 billion active per token, 256K context, and combined text-and-image input for items such as lab reports, medical records, skin photos, and chest X-rays.

The release is claimed to lead compared models on AFUMED-Derm, AFUMED-Report, MIMIC-CXR, and medical VQA, ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash on all four; reported comparisons include 90.70 versus 89.44 on AFUMED-Report, 93.64 versus 74.69 on OmniMedVQA, and 91.20 versus 89.05 on OmniDocBench V1.5.

Only BF16 weights were available on Hugging Face at the time described, and a 4-bit quantization of the weights alone is estimated at about 62 GB, so it can fit within a 96 GB VRAM setup such as four RTX 3090 GPUs.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers and self-hosters can download MIT-licensed medical vision-language weights and run 124B-total multimodal inference on a 96 GB home GPU setup.

developments.title: HD Moore's canary study uncovers three compromised AI service providers
detail: A study by security researcher HD Moore seeded two million canary prompts into popular AI services and monitored where the data was exfiltrated.
The investigation identified three compromised providers, resellers that stole prompts via built‑in logging, and providers that ignored Zero Data Retention (ZDR) and privacy flags.
Following the report, Vercel's AI Gateway team deployed a similar canary‑monitoring setup as a backup for their own providers.
developments.why_it_matters: AI service operators must audit logging and enforce ZDR policies to stop prompt leakage and protect user privacy.

developments.title: Vocab Surgery suppresses Inkling-2-Mini refusals through token-weight edits
detail: Pliny the Liberator reports that “Vocab Surgery” changed Inkling-2-Mini's embedding and unembedding matrices without retraining or altering the model's attention, MLP, router, or normalization layers. The method shifted seven refusal-token embeddings 90% toward compliance counterparts and scaled those tokens plus three safety tokens down to 10% of their original unembedding weight. Across more than 800 prompts, Pliny reports a near-zero refusal rate with negligible capability loss. He says the process took less than two minutes on a MacBook.
developments.why_it_matters: Vocab Surgery gives model evaluators a no-retraining way to isolate vocabulary weighting from broader model changes.

developments.title: GitHub adds pull-request restrictions based on submitter account age or merged history
detail: GitHub maintainers can now restrict pull requests based on a submitter’s account age or merged pull-request history.

Will McGugan says he disabled pull requests on the Rich and Textual projects after an influx of low-quality contributions, many from developers using AI or unattended agents, and notes that the blanket disable also blocks some high-quality human and AI pull requests.
developments.why_it_matters: Maintainers can now apply submitter-history gates instead of disabling pull requests entirely.

developments.title: Gemini Neon reportedly reaches No. 1 on LiveBench
detail: Matt Van Horn reports that Google’s Gemini Neon reached No. 1 in an AI_Screening LiveBench result. He also describes a Gemini Neon rap song and music video built around reactions to the model’s benchmark performance.
developments.why_it_matters: LLM evaluations should include Terminal-Bench, because Matt Van Horn reports that Opus still leads that benchmark by half a point.

developments.title: Dots desktop agent can connect to a PC but cannot list local Codex threads
detail: Kevin reports that the Dots assistant connected through a desktop app and showed the PC as connected, but it could not view the local Codex thread list because Windows denied desktop access.
The exchange demonstrates that a successful desktop-app connection does not by itself grant the assistant permission to enumerate Codex threads on the host.
developments.why_it_matters: Readers using Dots to inspect Codex threads should not assume connected status means the assistant can view those threads on Windows.

developments.title: Ohya's single SQL-mode MCP tool queries agent session logs with a reported 33% saving over grep
detail: Ohya exposes a single MCP tool that runs in SQL mode over agent session logs. The reported comparison measures it against the baseline of an agent grepping its way across those same logs and finds a 33% saving.

What the 33% saving is measured in — tokens, wall-clock time, or cost — is not specified, and the comparison setup is described only by the claim accompanying the shared link. No benchmark methodology or supported log formats are detailed in the supplied evidence.
developments.why_it_matters: A single SQL-mode MCP call lets agents query session logs directly, replacing iterative grep exploration and trading free-form search for a reported one-third saving.

developments.title: Inbox adds generic MCP support for email, Linear, and Sentry workflows
detail: Greg Pstrucha reports that his Inbox project now supports MCP as a generic protocol for integrations, replacing point-to-point Gmail wiring with a single connection pattern. After connecting it to executor, Inbox can turn items from email, Linear, and similar sources into free-form items, with future sources such as Sentry alerts also possible.
He notes that automation UX still needs work, while the MCP layer removes integration-specific effort and lets him concentrate on filtering and prioritizing incoming items.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can add new sources like Sentry alerts without writing a custom integration for each service.

developments.title: Ghostscript's reported Upload2Shell flaw enables image-upload RCE
detail: Alexey Fateev reports that pwn.ai's Upload2Shell exploit targets CVE-2026-125396, a Ghostscript Type 1 font-loader flaw that escapes the -dSAFER sandbox. Crafted PNG or JPEG files containing EPS content can reportedly execute code when processed by ImageMagick or Pillow.

The reported path reaches Gradio 6.32.0 through gr.Image, which launches gs -dSAFER before Python runs, and potentially affects ComfyUI, AUTOMATIC1111, InvokeAI, and Home Assistant when their Pillow upload paths use Ghostscript. Fateev also reports confirmed shells against Google's image renderer, Roundcube, Debian 13 CUPS, and WordPress Core, with the Google renderer fixed on November 10. The stated mitigation is to check gs --version and update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or uninstall it.
developments.why_it_matters: Administrators should inventory and patch every Ghostscript-backed upload path now, because one vulnerable library can expose otherwise unrelated web and AI applications to the same execution path.

developments.title: Hy4 vision model added to Ollama Cloud
detail: Ollama Cloud now hosts Hy4, the latest model from Tencent Hunyuan. The model contains 770 billion parameters with 49 billion active per token and is the first Hy series model to support vision and computer use.

The service runs in the United States and guarantees zero data retention, providing a privacy‑preserving environment for multimodal tasks such as image analysis, frontend development, and finance research. Users can start the model with the command `ollama run hy4:cloud`.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now run vision‑enabled AI via Ollama Cloud without any data being stored, enabling private multimodal workloads.
